name: Haggai
bio:
Haggai the prophet, together with Zechariah son of Iddo, prophesied to the Jews of Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel, encouraging Zerubbabel and Jeshua to resume building the temple after years of delay; the two prophets helped them as the work went forward (Ezra 5:1-2). His own messages are recorded in full in the book that bears his name. Through their prophesying, the elders of the Jews prospered in the work and finished the temple in the sixth year of Darius, dedicating it with joy (Ezra 6:14-16).

## 📖 Core Story: Rebuking the People's Priorities

In the second year of Darius, Haggai confronted the people for living comfortably in finished houses of their own while the LORD's temple lay in ruins, telling them their poor harvests and persistent want were the LORD's judgment for this neglect. Zerubbabel, Joshua the high priest, and the people obeyed and resumed the work (Haggai 1:1-15). A month later, Haggai encouraged the discouraged builders, who remembered the temple's former glory, promising that the LORD's Spirit remained with them and that this latter house would ultimately be filled with greater glory than Solomon's, with the treasures of all nations and lasting peace (Haggai 2:1-9). Using a priestly ruling on ritual purity, he taught that the people's own uncleanness had defiled even their offerings, but declared that from the very day the temple's foundation was relaid, the LORD would bless them (Haggai 2:10-19). In a final oracle, he pronounced Zerubbabel the LORD's chosen signet ring among the nations, a sign of special favor amid coming upheaval among the kingdoms (Haggai 2:20-23).
